Hi Sarah — really appreciate the clear asks and the attachments. Looping in Karthik (applied ML / quantization) and Monica (sales ops) so we can put together a pragmatic pilot commercial + technical guidance.

High level answers up front:
- For a pilot at 10M tokens/mo with soft latency, we usually recommend the "Efficiency Pilot" packaging: fixed monthly credits that cover baseline inference + a per-token overage rate. That lets you control spend while we instrument caching/batching savings.
- Prefix/KV caching typically reduces token compute by ~30–60% depending on prompt repetition. For ~80% repeated queries I'd expect toward the upper end (~50–60%), but we should validate against your prompt mix.
- Int8 is generally low risk; int4 can give 2–3x cost reduction on some stacks but may introduce hallucination or tokenization artifacts for chat prompts. Suggested rollout: start int8 on non-critical routes, validate log-likelihood/response fidelity with our eval harness, then consider int4 on read-only or retrieval-augmented flows.

Karthish, Monica — can you each provide short bullet answers (ops + technical) within EOD? We'll produce a pilot commercial (3-month credits + success criteria) and a recommended technical checklist.

Hi all — quick technical notes from my side. I used Sarah's pilot spreadsheet to estimate the impact; these are conservative: 

- Batching: for median request sizes you're likely to see ~15–30% per-token cost improvement from continuous batching on our runtime at 250–400ms SLOs, assuming request concurrency > 8. If concurrency is low, the gains are smaller.

- KV / prefix caching: the 50–60% figure Marcus mentioned is realistic if your 80% repeated queries are exact or have small suffix additions. If repetition is fuzzy, it drops to ~25–40%. We recommend capturing a 48–72 hour sample of live requests to run our cache-hit simulator.

- Quantization: int8 (we use Q8 variants) — negligible user-visible delta in 85%+ of chat prompts; safe as default. Int4: expect 5–12% drop in BLEU/ROUGE-style metrics on open prompts; hallucination risk rises on long-context summarization. Rollout plan: 
  1) Evaluate on stored prompt set (we can run this for you),
  2) Deploy int8 to 10% traffic with A/B evaluation,
  3) If metrics are stable, escalate to 50% and then full. For int4, keep it to offline/low-risk routes initially.

- Success metrics for pilot (recommended): response token perplexity delta < 3% vs baseline, user-rated acceptability >= 90% of baseline, and cache hit rate >= 40% after warm-up.

I'll attach a mini-runbook we use for pilots (ops steps + evaluation commands) — see Drive link in the hubspot record. If you want, we can run a short evaluation on a 5k-prompt sample from your dataset (we'll need scrubbed samples).

—Karthik
